title: Attic Conversion: Three Numbers That Decide Everything
description: Turning an attic into a real room: minimum ridge height, roof pitch, floor load capacity and daylight. A practical guide plus how to visualise the layout first.
excerpt: The attic is the last big space most people leave empty — and the cheapest room you will ever add to a house.
content:
The attic is the last big space most people leave empty. It is also the cheapest room you will ever add, because the walls and roof already exist.

## Measure three numbers first

**Ridge height** — you need at least 2.3 m, ideally 2.5 m. Below 2 m it will never be a living space, only storage.

**Roof pitch** — at 35° and steeper you get usable floor area near the walls. Below 30°, almost everything disappears under the slope.

**Floor load capacity** — the original ceiling joists were sized for boxes, not for a bed, a bookshelf and two adults. This one goes to a structural engineer, not to YouTube.

## Daylight decides the rest

Roof windows deliver roughly twice the light of a vertical window of the same size. Mount them lower than anyone suggests — bottom edge 110-120 cm above the floor, so you can see out while sitting.

A white ceiling and a pale floor add a psychological metre to the room. Dark timber on the slope does the opposite.

## Work with the slope, not against it

Put the things that do not need height underneath it: the bed, low built-in storage, a desk, a reading nook. Keep the centre of the room clear — that is where you walk.

## Test it before you call the builders

A conversion costs a small fortune and the layout gets decided once. Upload a photo of the bare attic to [RoomFlip](https://roomflip.io) and generate a few versions — bedroom, studio, kids' room. Five minutes tells you what actually works, and saves you three meetings.
